title: Magic Without Entanglement: Exact Revivals and Their Fisher Information Origin
abstract: Magic and entanglement are independent quantum resources, yet their exact relation in many-body dynamics has remained elusive. We uncover two structural principles. First, at any stabilizer state, the curvature of the second stabilizer Rényi entropy under an arbitrary Hermitian generator equals the quantum Fisher information up to a fixed normalization, creating a bidirectional bridge between computational and metrological resources. Second, for commuting Ising evolution on any forest graph, a Clifford pruning circuit yields the full stabilizer-Rényi family at arbitrary size and in any spatial embedding, thereby furnishing a graph-theoretic construction of families with finite magic density and vanishing entanglement density in the thermodynamic limit. We solve two paradigmatic one-dimensional realizations central to quantum simulation -- an Ising quench and a kicked Floquet chain -- exactly for arbitrary system size and directly in the thermodynamic limit, revealing finite magic density with vanishing entanglement density, distinct magic and entanglement revival periods, and Clifford points with zero magic but finite bipartite entanglement. The same tangent geometry fixes initial growth, perturbative revival lifting, and stability of thermodynamic magic minima. Large-scale Pauli-basis matrix-product-state calculations verify all predictions, and the tangent bridge yields a concrete protocol for detecting magic through established quantum-Fisher-information measurements.
summary: This work develops theoretical principles showing how 'Magic' and Entanglement behave independently in many-body systems undergoing time evolution. By analyzing specific 1D models, the authors prove that magic resources can survive when entanglement vanishes in the thermodynamic limit. The paper provides concrete mathematical bridges linking local resource measures like QFI to measurable quantities like Rényi entropy curvature.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish an exact framework connecting 'Magic' (a non-Clifford quantum resource) and Entanglement in the dynamics of many-body quantum systems.
main_result: It proves that for certain graph structures, finite magic density can persist even when entanglement density vanishes in the thermodynamic limit. Furthermore, it establishes a local relationship between Quantum Fisher Information and the curvature of the second stabilizer Rényi entropy at revival points.
method: The authors employ theoretical tools like stabilizer Rényi entropies ($M_\alpha$), Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), and graph-theoretic constructions (Forest Theorem) to analyze time evolution in the thermodynamic limit.
model_or_system: The study analyzes quantum many-body systems using models such as the Ising quench, kicked Floquet chains, and general commuting Ising dynamics on forest graphs. The analysis is performed for 1D spin chains.
key_observables: Magic density ($\mu_2$), Entanglement Entropy ($S_{EE}$), Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) curvature, and revival periods.
important_parameters: System size ($L 	o \infty$ limit), detunings ($\delta, \eta, \epsilon$), and the structure of the underlying graph (forest vs. cyclic).
main_assumptions: The tangent relation is a local, quadratic-order statement; the forest theorem applies specifically to acyclic graphs.
figures_summary: Figures compare normalized magic density revivals against entanglement entropy for quench and Floquet dynamics, showing distinct revival patterns and confirming predicted initial quadratic growth rates.
paper_structure: The paper develops structural theorems (Tangent Theorem, Forest Theorem) relating local resource measures. It applies these to 1D models (Ising quench, kicked chain), deriving exact results for density revivals and analyzing the stability of these minima using variance calculations in the thermodynamic limit.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, quantitative diagnostic tool (QFI vs. Magic) that can be measured experimentally or simulated to characterize non-equilibrium quantum dynamics beyond simple entanglement measures.
